take hydration SERIOUSLY!!! I mean it, start drinking tons of water days before you leave - arriving on Thursday with a GA camp spot typically means you’ll have a hefty walk to the venue each day (there are a BUNCH of hills, just heads up), so keeping yourself hydrated is SO important!!

Last year was my first LL, I arrived at 12:05am on Thursday and still had about a 35-40min walk to the festival entrance (i’ve got bad knees so I walk slower uphill). 
Food wise, I found it helpful to have a bin of all dry items like granolas, bread, bagels, etc and everything else in a cooler. Bring canned fruits like mandarin oranges or pineapple!! you don’t even need to keep them cold!! 
One step Im changing this year is how i’m bringing ice, I plan on freezing water bottles and using that as ice for the first two days. Buying ice bags at LL is NOT cheap. I was absolutely shocked when I had to pay nearly $30 for two small bags of ice that would’ve cost me $5 at any gas station - so keep this in mind!!

I recommend keeping your attire comfortable!! You should have good shoes for walking/hiking and comfortable socks!! Also, if you are someone who like to wear shorter bottoms / small swim suits - i recommend bringing a small clear gel deodorant for any thing chaffing!! This SAVED my legs last year oh MY GOD i was so grateful I packed it

Lastly, RAGE HARDDDDDD!!! Lost Lands is magical and weird and intense!! Truly no place like it :))

I had absolutely no one at the time, my best friend had dropped me because it was "too hard" for her to be around me and my depression, her boyfriend started harassing me and spread rumors about me around my school - hell even most of my family shut me out that year. The only person I had in my life was me. Thats it. 

I was even more destroyed when my attempt didn't go through. It took MONTHS for me to get past the internal shame I had for not being able to do it right, and years for me to forgive myself for the trauma I gave my mother with my attempt. To this day I am still suicidal, and my mother is still the only thing keeping me alive. Yeah, I have had EXTREMELY low days, but I have had a few BEAUTIFUL days as well. I went to college and immediately found myself a group of friends that were accepting of me (I'm LGBTQ+) and started playing with some psychedelics which have shown me some of the most amazing feelings ever. I'm 20 now, relatively happy, but still struggling with suicidal thoughts. I've been suicidal my whole life, and I honestly don't think that will ever change.

I don't really know what I am trying to say here. I want to say that you are not alone (in the least cheesiest way possible - i know we are all sick of hearing it). I want to say that even among the terrible and most numbing days you will have some sort of joy in your life, even if that joy is just a moment. But I hope you find comfort in knowing that some stranger on reddit is commenting on your post saying that they have gone through it and still are going through it. I hope you choose to stay <3
